tasks.short: Keep shipping supplies available, record stock and arrange replenishment.

steps.what: Count shipping supplies and inspect their condition at packing stations.
Enter counts and damaged quantities into the supplies register.
Compare stock, recent usage and delivery times to calculate replenishment needs.
Adjust replenishment for upcoming demand and approve the purchase requisition.
Check delivered supplies, restock packing stations and report discrepancies.

tasks.design: Configure a mobile count form in the {OPS_SYSTEM} so counts update the supplies register directly. A deterministic job combines packing volumes, stock, open orders and lead times to draft requisitions in the {PROCUREMENT}; the warehouse lead approves them before purchasing proceeds. Physical inspection, receipt checks and restocking remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Consumption is often poorly recorded, packaging units differ, and physical counts arrive separately from purchasing records.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing count forms and purchasing approvals cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding makes the remaining unit conversions and data connections cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Unrecorded waste, partial packs, supplier substitutions and physically moving supplies remain difficult to automate cheaply.
tasks.human_edge: Notice damaged materials and packing problems, and anticipate demand changes absent from recorded usage.

ambition.what: Weekly packaging safety-stock adjustments before promotion launches

tasks.altitude: The merchant spends less time copying counts and calculating quantities. The warehouse lead can gain delegated authority to adjust safety stock within an agreed working-capital limit.

reach.task: Compare packaging material use and damage rates across order types.
reach.learn: Packaging suitability, material measurement and the evidence needed for environmental claims.

evidence.claim: Stock registers, reorder calculations and requisition routing can use deterministic software.
Physical counting, inspection and restocking still require people without additional handling equipment.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.

assumptions: Reference workflow for a mid-size online retailer with an internal packing operation.
The build covers supplies tracking and requisition preparation; downstream purchasing remains a connected workflow.
No worker performance monitoring is proposed. GDPR applies to personal data; consultation follows applicable national rules.
unknowns: Whether shipping supplies are recorded in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, a workbook or an external warehouse's records.
Actual count accuracy, packing units, waste and replenishment lead times.
Available interfaces and purchasing approval limits.
Required access approvals and any applicable employee consultation.
research_questions: Does the existing {OPS_SYSTEM} already support mobile supplies counts and reorder thresholds?
Can packing events estimate consumption accurately enough to reduce count frequency?
new_work: Investigate differences between estimated consumption and physical counts.
Maintain packing units, supplier lead times and reorder thresholds.
Monitor failed register updates and duplicate requisitions.

tasks.short: Analyze website usage and search performance to choose improvements to discovery and conversion.

steps.what: Retrieve website usage reports from the web analytics service.
Retrieve query, ranking and landing-page reports from the search performance service.
Reconcile usage and search exports with order data, checking tracking gaps.
Calculate search trends, conversion funnels and performance by device and landing page.
Interpret findings and agree which search or interface hypothesis to test.
Write the experiment brief with scope, measures and implementation owner.

tasks.design: Scheduled connectors load website usage and search performance from {OTHER}, plus orders from the {ECOMMERCE}, into the {DATA_PLATFORM}. Deterministic checks flag tracking gaps and feed a {BI} dashboard; a template generates an experiment brief from the merchant's selected hypothesis. The merchant chooses the test, and implementation follows its own approval process.
tasks.previous_blocker: Separate exports, inconsistent landing-page identifiers and changing tracking definitions make repeated analysis expensive.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing connectors and dashboards cover collection and reporting. Small custom reconciliation jobs can now be built faster without needing a model to interpret every session.
tasks.still_hard: Consent-related measurement gaps, attribution uncertainty, seasonality and low traffic limit causal conclusions.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a tracking defect from a customer problem and choose a useful experiment under commercial constraints.

ambition.what: Weekly selection of a mobile checkout improvement experiment

tasks.altitude: The merchant reviews exceptions and experiments instead of rebuilding reports. A delegated experiment budget would let them choose small tests without escalating every brief.

reach.task: Prioritize landing-page improvements using query demand and conversion evidence.
reach.learn: Search intent, attribution limits and the difference between ranking changes and commercial impact.

reach.task: Turn funnel problems into accessible interface experiments.
reach.learn: Usability research, experiment design and accessible checkout patterns.

evidence.claim: Scheduled extraction, reconciliation and funnel calculations can be implemented deterministically.
Observed website correlations do not establish the effect of a proposed interface change.
The supplied digest contains no task-specific implementation case; effort estimates remain provisional.

assumptions: The reference design uses aggregate reports and excludes individual customer profiling.
Existing connectors are configured first; custom code handles only missing joins and quality checks.
Build ranges cover a first website and reporting model, including access and privacy review.
GDPR and applicable national tracking rules govern collection. This deterministic design does not require a model loop.
unknowns: Actual web analytics and search performance services, retention settings and export permissions.
Whether order and usage totals can be reconciled under current consent settings.
Traffic volumes, baseline conversion rates and available experiment infrastructure.
Who can approve experiments and whether employee consultation is relevant to the proposed collection.
research_questions: Which required metrics can the existing {BI} calculate without custom code?
Which tracking gaps materially change decisions?
What experiment duration would support a useful decision at the available traffic level?
new_work: Investigate tracking anomalies and broken connectors.
Maintain metric definitions and landing-page mappings.
Review experiment outcomes, including inconclusive results.
Check access, aggregation and retention settings as data sources change.

tasks.short: Revise the online business plan across assortment, pricing, stock and marketing investment.

steps.what: Collect sales, margin, stock and marketing results for the planning period.
Review market research, customer feedback and supplier constraints for planning implications.

loop.input: An approved set of research, aggregated feedback and supplier documents.
loop.output: A planning evidence brief with source references, dates, constraints and conflicting findings.
loop.check: Every factual statement must reference a supplied passage; the merchant checks material findings and omissions.
loop.stop: One extraction pass and one correction pass per document, capped at 30 documents per run; unresolved items go to the merchant.
loop.why_not_simpler: Relevant constraints and feedback appear in varied prose that fixed field mappings cannot reliably extract.

steps.what: Model assortment, price, inventory and marketing scenarios using explicit assumptions.
Choose the proposed commercial direction and resolve trade-offs with finance and marketing.
Draft the business plan with targets, actions, dependencies and risks.

loop.input: The selected scenario, decision rationale, reviewed evidence and fixed plan template.
loop.output: A draft plan that separates supported facts, assumptions, proposed actions and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Code checks all financial figures against the scenario model; the merchant reviews claims, feasibility and source references.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision, capped at 6,000 output words in total; unsupported sections remain flagged for manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates can insert figures, but explaining the chosen trade-offs requires bounded synthesis of prose and decisions.

steps.what: Approve the plan, resource envelope and accountable delivery owners.

tasks.design: A job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} assembles commercial results from the {ECOMMERCE}, {ERP}, {OPS_SYSTEM} and {ADS}, then fills a deterministic scenario model. Bounded loops extract cited evidence from approved {DOCS} and draft a plan only after the merchant selects a scenario. The commercial director approves the plan and resource envelope; spending remains subject to its existing approvals.
tasks.previous_blocker: Planning combines inconsistent figures, scattered research and narrative writing. Automating the document alone leaves assumptions and strategic choices unresolved.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable data mappings and scenario code reduce repeated preparation. Bounded extraction and drafting can use supplied evidence while leaving calculations deterministic.
tasks.still_hard: Demand assumptions, competitor responses, funding trade-offs and uncertain supplier capacity cannot be validated by producing a polished plan.
tasks.human_edge: Choose which commercial risk to take, challenge assumptions and secure commitments from finance, marketing and operations.

ambition.what: Monthly reassessment of assortment investment against cash and margin constraints

tasks.altitude: The merchant spends more of the planning week comparing options and negotiating commitments. Delegated authority could let them rebalance assortment investment within the approved resource envelope.

reach.task: Translate commercial scenarios into category campaign budgets and targets.
reach.learn: Contribution margin, incrementality and the effect of inventory constraints on campaign economics.

reach.role: Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists
reach.task: Design research to resolve a specific demand assumption before investment.
reach.learn: Sampling, uncertainty and how to distinguish stated interest from purchasing behaviour.

evidence.claim: Financial scenarios can use deterministic calculations while people choose assumptions and commercial direction.
The digest documents a generated report containing non-existent references, supporting explicit source checks for planning drafts.
The digest provides no business-plan automation outcome for this occupation; effort and build ranges are estimates.

assumptions: The first build covers one business unit, one planning template and a limited set of scenarios.
Models receive approved documents and aggregated customer feedback; confidential data stays within approved processing arrangements.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply where relevant. No employee scoring or automated resource commitments are proposed.
Access and consultation estimates cover initial review; applicable national procedures can extend elapsed rollout time.
unknowns: Actual source systems, metric consistency and availability of contribution-margin data.
Who owns planning assumptions and approval of the resource envelope.
Approved model processing arrangements, document access and retention requirements.
Applicable employee consultation and the scope of any delegated investment authority.
research_questions: Which scenario inputs most strongly change the investment decision?
Can the existing {BI} or {SPREADSHEET} support the required scenarios through configuration?
Can reviewers trace every material draft claim to a source or explicit assumption?
new_work: Review extracted evidence and unsupported claims.
Maintain scenario formulas, source mappings and planning templates.
Refresh assumptions and compare forecasts with actual outcomes.
Monitor model access, drafting quality and correction rates.

tasks.short: Publish accurate merchant details and approved transaction terms across online and offline materials.

steps.what: Retrieve and verify approved merchant identity, contact and registration details.
Select current transaction policies for the market, goods and sales channel.
Assemble merchant details and selected policies into online and offline disclosure drafts.
Review changed disclosures and authorize the exact release version.
Publish approved disclosures to storefront pages and transaction templates.
Insert approved disclosures into printable transaction materials.
Check rendered disclosures and retain publication evidence.

tasks.design: Keep versioned merchant details, approved clauses and market rules in the {DOCS}, with deterministic templates assembling each disclosure release. A named legal adviser authorizes the exact version through the {WORKFLOW}; publication to the {ECOMMERCE} and generation of print materials then use only that approved content. Automated completeness and version checks retain publication evidence and flag rendering defects for review.
tasks.previous_blocker: Merchant details and policies are copied across templates, while approvals in the {EMAIL} are difficult to tie to the version actually published.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned content, template generation and existing publishing controls already provide the necessary components. Small integrations can connect approval records to exact release versions.
tasks.still_hard: Legal applicability varies by market, goods and channel. Approved wording can still become unreadable or misplaced in a transaction journey.
tasks.human_edge: Decide whether terms accurately describe the transaction and whether customers can understand material restrictions before buying.

ambition.what: A reusable disclosure readiness check for new sales channels

tasks.altitude: The merchant manages release readiness and exceptions instead of repeatedly copying terms. They can gain authority to schedule publication within a legal adviser's approved release scope; legal interpretation remains with the adviser.

reach.task: Structure approved policies into reusable, readable disclosure modules.
reach.learn: Content modelling, version control and how to preserve legal meaning across formats.

reach.task: Prepare market-specific disclosure versions from approved source text.
reach.learn: Controlled terminology, locale requirements and review of legally meaningful differences.

evidence.claim: Approved clauses and structured merchant details can be assembled through deterministic templates without generating new legal wording.
Version-linked approval and publication checks can reduce mismatches between approved and published disclosures.
The digest supplies no disclosure-publishing implementation case; effort and build ranges are estimates.

assumptions: The first build covers one storefront and a limited set of approved print templates.
Legal advisers supply validated clauses and applicability rules; automation stops when no approved rule matches.
The release approval covers the exact online and print content, destinations and publication scope; subsequent delivery adds no discretion.
EU consumer and data-protection requirements apply, alongside market-specific national rules. No model loop is proposed.
unknowns: Actual selling countries, customer types, goods and disclosure obligations.
Where authoritative merchant details and approved translations are maintained.
Who may authorize releases and which changes require renewed legal review.
Whether publishing interfaces support version checks, rollback and transaction-template updates.
Required access approvals and any applicable employee consultation.
research_questions: Can existing {ECOMMERCE} templates reference one approved disclosure source?
Which disclosures need transaction-specific values rather than static text?
Can publication checks verify visibility and completeness across mobile, checkout and print layouts?
new_work: Maintain the approved clause library and market applicability rules.
Review unfamiliar transaction types and changed legal requirements.
Resolve rendering defects and failed publications.
Retire outdated templates and retain evidence of released versions.

role.altitude: The online merchant shifts from copying records and assembling reports toward stock exceptions, commercial experiments and investment choices. Approval rights expand only through explicit delegation of stock limits, experiment budgets and resource envelopes.
reach: Search Marketing Strategists: connect query demand to landing-page investment.
Web and Digital Interface Designers: turn funnel evidence into accessible experiments.
Marketing Managers: connect campaign budgets to margin and stock constraints.
Technical Writers: maintain reusable, versioned disclosure content.
Sustainability Specialists: measure packaging use alongside product protection.
skills_to_grow: Source verification and bounded model review
role.ambitious_version: Run a regular commercial review that combines search demand, conversion, stock availability and contribution margin to choose one funded improvement at a time, then compare its outcome with the original hypothesis.
